title: Harvesting tomatoes
subtitle: When to pick, ripening late-season green fruit, and what to do at the end of summer
excerpt: Tomatoes are ready to pick from July onwards when fully coloured and slightly soft to the touch. In a typical UK summer, a proportion of fruit will still be green by September; green tomatoes can be ripened indoors or used for chutney. Clearing the plants before the first frost prevents blight carrying over.
sourceNotes: RHS tomato growing guide (rhs.org.uk). Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), kitchen garden section. USDA cooperative extension notes on tomato production, public domain.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cluster of tomatoes growing from a single stem on a cordon tomato plant. Each truss forms a flower cluster that ripens into a group of fruits. On a well-grown cordon tomato, each truss typically contains four to eight fruits. Counting trusses is a useful guide to removing the growing tip at the end of the season: in a UK summer, pinch out the tip above the fourth or fifth truss in August to redirect energy into ripening existing fruit.

content.text: upwards. The first fruits to ripen are the lowest ones; pick as they reach full colour and slight give. Don't leave ripe tomatoes on the plant; they divert energy from the fruit above and are at risk from splitting in rain.

Pick when the fruit has reached full colour for its variety and gives slightly when pressed. Tomatoes picked at this stage and brought indoors at room temperature will improve further over two or three days. Never store tomatoes in the refrigerator; cold below 12°C destroys the volatile compounds that give ripe tomatoes their flavour. Pick even if you have more than you can eat immediately; process the excess into sauce, soup, or dried tomatoes.
End of season: pinching out and ripening

In August, pinch out the growing tip of cordon tomatoes above the fourth or fifth truss, leaving two leaves above the top truss. This stops the plant setting new flowers and redirects energy into ripening the existing fruit. Remove all remaining flowers. Bush tomatoes do not need pinching out.

In most UK years, a proportion of tomatoes will still be green by mid-September. Green tomatoes will ripen indoors at room temperature if placed on a windowsill or in a warm place; this can take two to four weeks. Adding a ripe apple or banana to a bag with the green tomatoes releases ethylene and speeds ripening. Alternatively, use green tomatoes for green tomato chutney; the flavour is excellent.

Remove all tomato plants by mid-October, before the first hard frost. Do not compost any plant material that has shown blight symptoms; bag and bin it. Healthy plants can go on the compost. Clear all foliage from the greenhouse to reduce overwintering pest populations.
